clue.text: Ear of horse with hard growth on the front

indicators.note: placing one piece on the front of another tells you which comes first in the answer

parts.note: a corn is a patch of hardened skin on the foot
a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse

explanation.surface: A horse with a hard lump growing on the front of its ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ear of horse' reads as a body part; the definition is just 'Ear', and the horse belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the whole seed head of maize, which is also called an ear of corn.

clue.text: Like a shellfish, might you say, sticky and damp?

indicators.note: asking how you might say it means the word is judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: an adjective for being like a clam, a shellfish

explanation.surface: Is something sticky and damp like a shellfish?
explanation.walkthrough: A clam is a shellfish, so 'clam-y' would mean clam-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy describes skin or air that is unpleasantly moist and sticky to the touch.

clue.text: Freshly arrange record in shelf

indicators.note: one item placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a rack is a shelf or frame for storing things
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone rearranges a record on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack is to pack again, putting the contents back in a new arrangement.

clue.text: Ben Hur for one a wildly enjoyable event — applause all round

indicators.note: a word placed all round another wraps it, holding it inside

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of applause
taken as written
a riot is a highly entertaining occasion

explanation.surface: Ben Hur is hailed as a thrilling spectacle, with applause all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildly enjoyable event' sounds like a description of the film, but it is a colloquial word for a great time. Ben Hur raced chariots in the famous film.
explanation.definitionFit: Judah Ben-Hur, hero of the novel and film, drives a chariot in its famous race, making him an example of a charioteer.

clue.text: Said to be one more than expected in golf trolley

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.words: to be one more than expected in golf
parts.note: a bogey is a hole played in one stroke over par

explanation.surface: A golfer's score of one over par, linked somehow to a golf trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf trolley' reads as a single item, but 'trolley' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogie is a wheeled undercarriage or low truck, the kind of trolley found under railway wagons.

clue.text: Hamper available that climber may need

parts.note: to cramp is to restrict or hamper
on, as in 'on offer', means available

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper is on hand for a climber who might want one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a picnic basket, but it is the verb meaning restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: A crampon is a spiked metal plate fixed to a boot, gear a mountaineer needs on ice.

clue.text: Composer has sweet child in India

parts.note: a sweet, angelic-looking child is called a cherub
taken as written
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A composer has a lovely child living in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a placing instruction, but it is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and sacred music who worked in Paris.

clue.text: To a degree, one may be master of these

definitions.text: To a degree, one may be master of these

parts.note: surface reading: to some extent, someone can master these skills
setter's reading: the university degree called a Master of these subjects

explanation.surface: Up to a point, a person can become skilled in certain things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' means somewhat, but it points to an academic degree: MA.
explanation.definitionFit: An MA is a Master of Arts, the postgraduate degree in humanities subjects.

clue.text: To which one does dad dancing?

definitions.text: To which one does dad dancing?

parts.note: surface reading: the awkward dancing of middle-aged fathers at parties
setter's reading: a father is a pop, and what one dances to is music

explanation.surface: What tune sets off embarrassing dad dancing?
explanation.walkthrough: Dad is POP, so the music that dad dancing is done to is literally pop's music.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop music is chart music, the commercial genre most often heard at parties and discos.

clue.text: Fail to get up to acknowledge formally

parts.note: failing to do something means not doing it
to arise is to get up

explanation.surface: Someone fails to stand to give a formal acknowledgement.
explanation.definitionFit: To notarise is to have a notary certify a document, a formal legal acknowledgement of it.

clue.text: First-class kind of brainwave

definitions.meaning: first meaning: top grade, from the first Greek letter
second meaning: a rhythm of electrical activity seen in a relaxed waking brain

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brainwave' suggests a sudden clever idea, but here it is the literal electrical wave measured in the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha marks the top grade (an alpha mark), and alpha waves are a recognised band of brain rhythm.

clue.text: What tea bag does is ruined

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a tea bag is put into a teapot
second meaning: the idiom for falling into decay

explanation.surface: A grumble that a tea bag spoils the brew.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally: the tea bag really does go into the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating or being spoiled, and a tea bag is dropped into a teapot.

clue.text: Staff receiving unexpectedly nice hug, but one is fired

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so the letters are jumbled
a word that is receiving something takes it inside itself

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: An employee is sacked for giving an unwelcome hug at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a noun for employees, but it is the verb meaning to man. 'Fired' in the surface means sacked; in the definition it means shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine gun is a firearm that is fired, shooting bullets in rapid succession.

clue.text: Losing energy, more refined sound from pet

indicators.note: a word that is losing something gives up a letter, here the one standing for energy

parts.note: purer means more refined
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A pet's sound grows less refined as it loses energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the E out of PURER to leave PURR.
explanation.definitionFit: A purr is the low contented vibrating noise a cat makes.

clue.text: Restrained right-winger attacked online

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative
to troll someone is to post abuse at them on the internet

explanation.surface: A right-wing figure kept calm despite abuse on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: Controlled means held in check, kept restrained.

clue.text: Accounts people boxed in have to give, after some swearing

definitions.text: Accounts people boxed in have to give, after some swearing

parts.note: surface reading: people shut in a box, perhaps prisoners or boxers, after an outburst of bad language
setter's reading: witnesses stand in the witness box and speak after swearing an oath in court

explanation.surface: People penned in somewhere have to explain themselves after cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: The box is the witness box, and the swearing is taking the oath, not cursing.
explanation.definitionFit: Testimonies are the statements witnesses give as evidence in court once they have been sworn in.

clue.text: A long read for the old folks' outing?

definitions.text: A long read for the old folks' outing?

parts.note: setter's reading: a lengthy book telling a family story over generations
surface reading: a book to take on a pensioners' holiday, with Saga as the UK travel company for the over-fifties

explanation.surface: A long book to take on a pensioners' trip away.
explanation.walkthrough: Saga is a British firm selling holidays to people over fifty, so its trips are the old folks' outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga novel is a long work following a family or community over many years, so a lengthy read.

clue.text: Some schools used to be ticked off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... schools were former British residential institutions for young offenders
second meaning: marked with a tick as accepted

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticked off' suggests scolded, but here it means checked and accepted. Approved schools were British reform schools, abolished in 1973.
explanation.definitionFit: Approved means officially accepted, as an item ticked off on a list, and was the name of a type of reform school.

clue.text: Special nuptial mass for recent jubilee

indicators.note: something made special is altered from its ordinary form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A special wedding mass is held to celebrate a recent jubilee.
explanation.walkthrough: The recent jubilee is Queen Elizabeth II's Platinum Jubilee of 2022, marking seventy years on the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A platinum jubilee marks a seventieth anniversary, and Elizabeth II celebrated hers in 2022.

clue.text: Let priest go casting out troublesome spirit

indicators.note: casting can mean shaping into a new form, so these letters are reworked into another order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, rearranged

explanation.surface: An exorcist priest is released after driving out a troublesome spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casting out' suggests exorcism, which fits the spirit perfectly, but it signals a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltergeist is a ghost blamed for noises and objects being thrown about, a troublesome spirit.

clue.text: Swinging both ways in pool, manifesting sexual impulse

indicators.note: something placed in another item is held inside it

parts.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool
bisexual, attracted to both sexes

explanation.surface: Someone bisexual at the swimming pool shows their sexual urges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinging' suggests motion or reversal, but the phrase is slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is the psychological term for sexual desire or drive.

clue.text: Inadequate? Some agree, but only some

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run of them sitting inside the phrase

parts.note: a run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Is it not enough? Some people agree, but only a few.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Some' into 'agree'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or quality, so insufficient.

clue.text: Book, not initially non-fiction

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: non-fiction deals in truth rather than invention

explanation.surface: A book that turns out not to be non-fiction at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the T from TRUTH. Ruth is a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is one of the books of the Bible, telling the story of Ruth and Naomi.

clue.text: Son finally getting wheels, but not on this

definitions.text: Son finally getting wheels, but not on this

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
at last having a car means you are now mobile

explanation.surface: A son at last gets a vehicle, though not a wheeled one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a vehicle that runs on skis and tracks rather than wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowmobile is a motor vehicle that travels over snow on skis and a track instead of wheels.

clue.text: Sausage of lowest quality for an audience

indicators.note: something for an audience is heard, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: the poorest is the worst

explanation.surface: Sausage of the poorest kind served up to listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Wurst is the German word for sausage, used in English for German-style sausages like bratwurst.

clue.text: Pass up a soft drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means placed higher, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass up' reads as decline, but 'up' only places the pass above A in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a sweet carbonated drink flavoured with kola nut, a classic soft drink.

clue.text: Vehicle needs insurance to go round university city

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: something set to go round another item surrounds it, holding it inside

parts.note: insurance cover
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A van has to be insured before it drives round a university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insurance' here is the cover a policy provides; the vehicle is simply placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Vancouver is a major city on the Pacific coast of British Columbia, Canada.

clue.text: Prone to dishonesty

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the habit of telling falsehoods

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prone to' reads as 'inclined to', but 'Prone' stands alone as horizontal and 'to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying can describe someone stretched flat on the ground, and also the act of telling untruths.

clue.text: Save nobody and nothing

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: condemn everyone, sparing no one
second meaning: the slang phrase for nothing at all

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'damn all' literally, as damning everyone, and you save nobody; as slang it means nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: Damn all is informal British slang for nothing at all, and taken word by word it means condemning every person.

clue.text: Young swimmer to plead being injured

indicators.note: something injured is knocked out of shape, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A junior swimmer pleads after getting hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval form of a frog or toad, which lives and swims in water.
